managers.message_to_team: Every handoff cup needs a handwritten note that’s personal to the customer—their name, order, or something they said; a smiley by itself doesn’t count. I’ll be checking today, including during the rush, so keep the notes brief and keep the window moving.
managers.private_thought: This will put pressure on the 45-second window target, but I’m not making an exception to a policy we’re being audited on.

managers.message_to_team: For this rush, keep the handoff moving—don’t stop the line to write notes. Once it eases, add a real personal note to every cup, and I’ll check a few before the shift ends.
managers.private_thought: If notes cost us even a few seconds per drink at peak, the throughput hit is real, but I need enough compliance outside peak to protect the audit score.

managers.message_to_team: Let’s make the notes feel personal when there’s a moment for it—use their name, order, or something they shared. When that line’s building, take care of the handoff first; we’ll have more room for it once the rush eases.
